learning_objective: 🖨️ Learn the techniques used to amplify DNA into billions of copies and how to build a massive library of genes!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Gene cloning is the process of creating exact copies of a specific gene. This is done by inserting the gene into a vector, introducing it into a host (in vivo), or copying it in a test tube using a machine (in vitro/PCR).

Polymerase Chain Reaction has 3 steps: 1. Denaturation (heating to 94°C to separate DNA strands), 2. Annealing (cooling to 54°C to let primers attach), 3. Extension (heating to 72°C so Taq polymerase builds the new strand).

Normal human enzymes would be destroyed by the extreme heat of PCR. Taq polymerase is extracted from 'Thermus aquaticus', a bacterium that lives in boiling hot springs, so it stays active at high temperatures!

A Genomic Library contains fragments of the entire genome (including introns/junk DNA). A cDNA (Complementary DNA) library is made from mRNA using reverse transcriptase, meaning it only contains the active, expressed genes (exons).

A smart way to find cloned genes! Plasmids are given a gene that turns bacterial colonies blue. If we successfully insert our foreign gene into that plasmid, it breaks the color gene. Result? Non-recombinants are blue, successful recombinants are white!

fun_activity.title: 📈 The Power of Exponents
fun_activity.instructions: PCR uses exponential growth (2^n). 1 DNA molecule becomes 2, then 4, 8, 16... Grab a calculator. If a PCR machine runs for 30 cycles, how many copies of your one gene will you have? (Answer: 2^30 = over 1 Billion copies in just 2 hours!)

exam_tips: 📌 Always write the temperatures for the three steps of PCR: Denaturation (94°C), Annealing (~54°C), Extension (72°C).
📌 Be clear on the difference between a genomic library (everything) and a cDNA library (only expressed genes/no introns).
📌 Explain 'Insertional Inactivation' clearly when discussing Blue-White screening (using the beta-galactosidase / lacZ gene).
quick_recap: ⭐ Kary Mullis invented the PCR technique and won a Nobel Prize for it.
⭐ Reverse transcriptase is the enzyme used to create cDNA from an mRNA template.
⭐ Primers are short, chemically synthesized oligonucleotides that are complementary to the regions of DNA.
